extracted.intended_audience: IB Mathematics students preparing their Internal Assessment (IA)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, writing, and scoring an IB Mathematics Internal Assessment (IA), explaining the five official criteria (A–E), achievement levels, and practical tips for SL and HL students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion A: Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Achievement Level Descriptor 0–4 where 4 = 'The exploration is coherent, well organized, and concise.' Evaluates coherence, organization, and conciseness of the IA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation evaluates how coherently and logically your work is organized and the succinctness of your communication. Focus on: Coherence (logical flow from one section to the next), Organization (clear sections with headings/subheadings and consistent layout), Conciseness (thorough yet brief; avoid unnecessary details). Examples given: Good Presentation — clear introduction, structured exploration/analysis, concise conclusion, headings and no redundant information. Poor Presentation — jumps randomly between topics, overly complex/confusing language, or irrelevant data that clutters main points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion B: Mathematical Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Achievement Level Descriptor 0–4 where 4 = 'The mathematical communication is relevant, appropriate, and consistent throughout.' Assesses use of appropriate mathematical language, symbols, notation, and clarity of explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate mathematical language and standard notation; define every variable and symbol. Tips: be clear and precise (explain each part of equations and what parameters represent), use visual aids (graphs, tables, diagrams) to clarify complex ideas, and provide step-by-step explanations for calculations or derivations so the reader can follow without leaps in logic. Avoid casual or non-mathematical usage of terms unless they directly apply. The page emphasizes explaining why methods/models are chosen and ensuring notation matches academic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion C: Personal Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Achievement Level Descriptor 0–3 where higher levels indicate increasing evidence of personal engagement (1 = some evidence, 3 = outstanding personal engagement). Measures the student's personal connection, initiative, creativity and curiosity in the IA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate personal interest and initiative: choose a topic you care about so passion shows, adopt an original approach (unusual application, novel modeling, interdisciplinary integration), connect the project to personal interests (e.g., sports statistics), describe innovative problem solving (new methods or use of software), and reflect on the process (challenges overcome). The IA should reflect your curiosity and investigative spirit, showing how you pushed beyond routine tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion D: Reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Achievement Level Descriptor 0–3 where higher levels indicate more substantial and critical reflection. Evaluates the student's ability to reflect on the process, results, implications, and personal/academic learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection should analyze both process and outcomes: discuss steps taken and evaluate their effectiveness, note unexpected hurdles or successes and how they influenced direction/results. Discuss implications of results beyond numbers (real-world consequences or meanings). Emphasize learning gains: personal growth (skills, perseverance), academic development (new software or deeper conceptual understanding), and propose future directions (additional variables to explore or alternative approaches). Thoughtful, critical reflection demonstrates deeper understanding and rounds out the IA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion E: Use of Mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Achievement Level Descriptor 0–6 where levels describe increasing correctness, relevance and depth of mathematics used (6 = 'Relevant mathematics commensurate with the level of the course is used. The mathematics explored is correct. Thorough knowledge and understanding are demonstrated.'). Assesses appropriateness, correctness, and sophistication of mathematics relative to SL/HL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mathematics appropriate to your level (SL: apply core concepts effectively; HL: deeper exploration and more advanced topics). Choose mathematical theories and techniques that naturally fit the investigation — avoid forced or irrelevant advanced math. Explain why methods are chosen and how they apply to the topic. Demonstrate mathematical rigor by showing step-by-step work everyone familiar with IB Math can follow, detailing calculations and how conclusions were reached. Avoid common pitfalls: over-simplifying complex concepts or using advanced mathematics incorrectly. Effective use of mathematics should enhance the investigation and provide clear, quantifiable insights aligned with the research question.
